title: Reverse Only the Vowels
statement: In `text`, reverse the **order of the vowels** and leave every other character where it is. The vowels are `a`, `e`, `i`, `o`, `u` in lower case and in upper case. Return the new text.

examples.explanation: The vowels, in order, are e, u, a, i, o. Reversed: o, i, a, u, e. They are put back into the vowel positions, the consonants stay.

hints.nudge: Swapping the first vowel with the last, the second with the second last, and so on reverses their order. How do you find the vowels to swap?
hints.pattern: Two pointers from both ends: move the left one right until it is on a vowel, move the right one left until it is on a vowel, swap, and continue.
hints.pseudocode:
chars = the letters of text; left = 0; right = n - 1
while left < right:
  if chars[left] is not a vowel: left += 1
  elif chars[right] is not a vowel: right -= 1
  else: swap chars[left] and chars[right]; left += 1; right -= 1
return the chars joined
hints.walkthrough: Collecting the vowels in a list, reversing the list and writing them back also works (two passes). With two pointers you do it in one pass and no extra list: the left pointer stops at the next vowel from the left, the right pointer at the next vowel from the right; swapping those two puts the first vowel where the last one was and the other way round. Then both pointers move on. A vowel in the middle that has no partner stays. Remember that capital letters count as vowels too (A, E, I, O, U), and the capital stays a capital because the characters themselves are swapped.
